newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay sugar prices rise on consumer buying.
newsitem.headline: Bombay sugar prices rise on consumer buying.

text.p: Indian sugar prices on Friday rose on fresh consumer buying while limited mill arrivals kept down offerings, dealers said.

Ready delivery S-30 sugar rose by 5/10 rupees at 1,440/1,470 rupees per quintal while sugar M-30 fell by five rupees at 1,475/1,505 rupees. Sugar mill delivery rose to 1,380/1,395 rupees per quintal from 1,375/1,390 rupees.

"Fears among traders that the Indian government may announce a lower free sale quota for next month also aided the firm tendency during the day," said Shantilal Dedhiya, secretary to Bombay Sugar Merchant Association.
He said the quota for July may be around 700,000/725,000 tonnes against 800,000 tonnes for the current month.
